nat.kid: {name} swaps the sender address for its own outside address, and remembers who asked.
nat.nerd: NAT: source {inside}:51034 is rewritten to {outside}:51034 and stored in the connection table.

unnat.kid: {name} looks up who asked for this and changes the address back to {yours}.
unnat.nerd: NAT reverse: destination {outside} is rewritten back to {inside} from the connection table.

bridge.kid: {name} doesn’t read the address. It just passes the parcel on.
bridge.nerd: {name} doesn’t route: it swaps the link frame for the next one and leaves this IP packet untouched.

read.kid: This box reads the address and picks the best way onwards.
read.nerd: Routed: longest-prefix match in the FIB, TTL − 1, a new link frame for the next hop.

arrived.kid: Arrived! This is the right address.
arrived.nerd: Destination reached: hand the payload up to TCP.
